original_value: Heart problems are responsible for the majority of deaths worldwide. The use of intelligent techniques to assist in the identification of existing patterns in these diseases can facilitate treatments and decision making in the field of medicine. This work aims to extract knowledge from a dataset based on heart noise behaviors in order to determine whether heart murmur predilection exists or not in the analyzed patients. A heart murmur can be pathological due to defects in the heart, so the use of an evolving hybrid technique can assist in detecting this comorbidity team, and at the same time, extract knowledge through fuzzy linguistic rules, facilitating the understanding of the nature of the evaluated data. Heart disease detection tests were performed to compare the proposed hybrid model’s performance with state of the art for the subject. The results obtained (90.75% accuracy) prove that in addition to great assertiveness in detecting heart murmurs, the evolving hybrid model could be concomitant with the extraction of knowledge from data submitted to an intelligent approach.

result.paraphrase: Heart disease is responsible for most deaths worldwide. Intelligent techniques can help identify patterns in these diseases, supporting treatment and medical decision-making. This work seeks to extract knowledge from a dataset of heart sound behavior to determine whether the analyzed patients have a predisposition to heart murmur. Because a heart murmur may be pathological and stem from heart defects, an evolving hybrid technique can aid in detecting this comorbidity while also extracting knowledge through fuzzy linguistic rules, which helps clarify the nature of the evaluated data. Heart disease detection tests compared the proposed hybrid model’s performance with the state of the art in the field. The results achieved, with 90.75% accuracy, show that the evolving hybrid model not only detects heart murmurs with high accuracy but can also simultaneously extract knowledge from data using an intelligent approach.
